resolvedSectionBreaks.before:
This relation is called Avogadro's law.
It is exact for ideal gases.
For real gases, it is approximate only where the ideal-gas approximation applies.
resolvedSectionBreaks.after:
According to Avogadro's law, at the same pressure $p$ and temperature $t$, $1$ mole of any ideal gas occupies the same volume.
This is because $1$ mole contains the same number of specified gas particles.

resolvedSectionBreaks.before:
This value is not a volume that remains unchanged at every temperature and pressure.
Always specify both conditions when comparing gas volumes.
resolvedSectionBreaks.after:
Here $V_{0\mathrm{m}}$ is the molar volume at the specified standard state.
Molar volume is volume per mole of gas, not the total volume of an arbitrary sample.
